title: Prime-Pairs Synchronization Prediction Algorithm 2026: Geometric Segment Dynamics, Endpoint Reuse, and Computational Experiments for Goldbach Representations
content: We introduce a prime-pair segment formalism for the binary Goldbach problem and an algorithmic framework for propagating verified or probable-prime decompositions between consecutive even integers. A segment [p,q] is associated with an even target E=p+q, center m=E/2, half-length d=m−p, and full length L=q−p=2d. A general transition (p,q)↦(p+2k,q+2−2k) preserves the sum E+2, with d↦d+1−2k. The special cases k=1 and k=0 preserve one endpoint and permit computational reuse of an existing primality result when the other endpoint is prime. We describe an auditable implementation with exact enumeration for moderate integers, window-limited searches for larger integers, and explicitly conditional probable-prime results near 10^2000.A supplementary dataset contains 304,259 recorded segment rows for 98 sampled even integers across six base scales. We emphasize that endpoint propagation is an exact identity but not an unconditional primality predictor. We cite twelve separately supplied figures and twelve tables, computational controls, failure modes, and a reproducibility agenda. No claim is made to prove the binary Goldbach conjecture or to exhaustively enumerate representations for enormous targets.
